gaps.sentence: The storm did considerable ___ to the harbour wall.
gaps.explanation: 'Do damage' — uncountable; 'damages' means money awarded in court.

gaps.sentence: A car remained ___ at the traffic lights for ages.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationary' means not moving; 'stationery' means pens, paper and other writing materials.

gaps.sentence: The committee acted on legal ___ before revising the clause.
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the noun; 'advise' is the verb.

gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: The two leaders signed a ___ peace agreement.
gaps.hint: important enough to be remembered in history
gaps.explanation: 'Historic' means important or famous in history; 'historical' just means connected with the past or the study of history.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.

gaps.sentence: The new regulations came into ___ last month.
gaps.explanation: 'Come into effect' means to start being used; 'affect' is a verb and cannot follow 'into'.
